'''Hintaro''' was a [[Chance cube/Legends|dice]] game for at least two players. It was played with chance cubes that were traditionally marked with the symbols "Tukar" and "Kulro," as well as a single unique die known as the [[Hintaro (chance cube)|hintaro]], which had the symbols "Hin" and "Taro" on it. During each round of the game, the players would each roll a pair of dice, one of which they could reroll. After each player had rolled, a special player called the [[hintaron]] would roll the hintaro. The result of that die modified the rolls of all the players, after which the winner of the round was determined.

The [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Chazwa/Legends|Chazwa]] and [[Corsin/Legends|Corsin]] both claimed to be the birthplace of hintaro, although the existence of a single origin point for the game was unlikely. Between [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]] and [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], hintaro was played at the [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] ''[[Four-and-a-Half]]'' on the planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin's]] [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]]. The [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[Big game hunter|hunter]] [[Kres'keth'errylu]] once played hintaro against an [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] at a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler's]] hideaway.

==Description==
===Prerequisites and variations===
Hintaro was a [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] game for at least two players that was played with six-sided [[Chance cube/Legends|chance cubes]]. A proper hintaro game was played with special dice that had unique symbols on their faces. A single, unique die known as the [[Hintaro (chance cube)|hintaro]] had multiple symbols named "Hin" and "Taro" on its faces, while each other die was marked with the same combination of the symbols "Tukar" and "Kulro." To play a game of hintaro, the players needed one hintaro die plus two of the regular dice per player. Simplified variants of the game substituted standard chance cubes for the unique hintaro dice.<ref name="Fly" />

Despite the existence of regional variations of hintaro, a set of standard rules for the game was generally abided by [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] and other communities that experienced a frequent flow of travelers. Additionally, differences existed between hintaro rules in [[Casino/Legends|casino]] and non-organized play.<ref name="Fly" />

===Round structure===
====Antes, rolls, and wagers====
[[File:Chancecube.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Standard chance cubes were sometimes used in hintaro.]]
Each hintaro game was comprised of several rounds, each of which consisted of six steps. In the first step, the players designated a special player known as the [[hintaron]], the role of which was similar to that of a dealer in card games. The hintaron was almost always the hintaro dealer in casino gambling. In contrast, the role of hintaron usually changed each round in non-organized gaming, with the duty typically passing to the person to the left of the previous hintaron.<ref name="Fly" />

In the second step of a hintaro round, each player, beginning with the player to the left of the hintaron, paid the ante to the pot to initiate the round. The ante from each player was collected by the hintaron. Each player threw two of the regular chance cubes in the third step of the game. The house rolled the cubes of each player in casino gaming, but the players usually threw the dice on their own in recreational play.<ref name="Fly" />

Beginning at the hintaron's right, each player could wager an additional amount in the fourth step. The next player had to either meet the new bet or drop out of the game. Finally, the hintaron made a decision to either meet the new wagers or raise, after which all the other players had to either meet or drop out. In the wager step, each player thus added their new bet, collected by the hintaron, to the pot.<ref name="Fly" />

====Rerolls and the hintaro====
In the penultimate step of a hintaro game round, the hintaron, starting with the player to their left, asked each player in turn whether they, having examined the other players' rolls, would reroll one of their own chance cubes. If the player did reroll at that point, they had to accept the new result no matter what. The goal of the reroll was to help the player obtain at least one pair of matching "Tukar" or "Kulro" symbols on their dice.<ref name="Fly" />

The hintaron threw the special hintaro die in the sixth and final step of the round. The result of the hintaro modified the rolls of all players, with each "Hin" and "Taro" symbol on the special chance cube canceling out each "Tukar" and "Kulro" symbol on the players' dice.<ref name="Fly" />

====Determining the winner====
Finally, the rank, if any, of the players' modified rolls was compared, allowing the round's winner to be determined. A result consisting of two "Tukar" and two "Kulro" symbols held the highest rank and was known as "Tukar to Kulro." The second-highest rank was held by a roll of four "Kulro" symbols, known as a "Quad Kulro." The third and fourth ranks were held by "Tukar Tukar" and "Kulro Kulro," which were held by a single pair of "Tukar" and "Kulro," respectively. Any other result rolled had no rank and could not win.<ref name="Fly" />

The player who had the roll with the highest rank won the match and the entire pot. The winnings were split in the case of a tie, and the pot remained in place for the next round if no one won.<ref name="Fly" />

==History==
[[File:Keth_EtU.png|thumb|right|200px|The Chiss big-game hunter Kres'keth'errylu once played hintaro.]]
Although both [[Chazwa/Legends|Chazwa]],<ref name="Fly" /> an [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]]<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Chazwa system/Legends|Chazwa system]] and [[Corsin system/Legends|Corsin system]]</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]], and [[Corsin/Legends|Corsin]], a world<ref name="Fly" /> in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]],<ref name="EAOC" /> claimed they were the birthplace of hintaro, the game eventually became popular on many worlds, and it was more likely that the game evolved out of several similar games with different points of origin.<ref name="Fly" /> Hintaro was among the games and other forms of entertainment available at the ''[[Four-and-a-Half]]'', an illegal [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] located in the [[Port Town (Cloud City)/Legends|Port Town]] district of the [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] [[City/Legends|settlement]] on the<ref name="Jewel" /> [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]],<ref name="Jewel" /> at some point between [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]] and [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="Jewel dates">{{JewelofYavindate}}</ref>

The [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[Big game hunter/Legends|big-game hunter]] [[Kres'keth'errylu]], known as Keth,<ref name="Enter">''[[Enter the Unknown]]''</ref> once played hintaro at an establishment<ref name="Fly" /> that served as a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler's]] hideaway.<ref name="Redemption">{{FFGTCG|set=Redemption and Return|cardname=Smuggler's Hideaway|link=endor-cycle/redemption-and-return/smuggler%e2%80%99s-hideaway-r1747}}</ref> The [[Hunting/Legends|hunter's]] opponent was<ref name="Fly" /> an old-model [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]],<ref name="Old droid">''[[Fly Casual]]'', which is set during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], depicts [[Kres'keth'errylu]] playing hintaro against a [[Droid/Legends|droid]], the type of which ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' identifies as an [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]]. ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the war to between [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]] and [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], while ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' places the events of ''Knights of the Old Republic'' in [[3956 BBY]].</ref> and the game was played with a set of [[Color/Legends|red]] dice. Both players had large stacks of gaming chips in front of them and had set their weapons down on the table they were playing at&mdash;a [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] in Keth's case and a [[Vibro-ax/Legends|vibro-ax]] lodged into the table's surface on the [[Droid/Legends|droid's]] side. Both the Chiss and the droid were standing up while playing the game, with an [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] carrying [[Foodstuff/Legends|beverage]] [[Glass/Legends|glasses]] on its dome-shaped head also present at the table. At one point during the game, the droid playing against Keth rolled dice on the table, with the hunter watching the throw intently.<ref name="Fly" />

==Behind the scenes==
Hintaro was introduced in ''[[The Jewel of Yavin]]'', a [[2014]] adventure supplement for [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire]]'' [[Star Wars Roleplaying|roleplaying game]] system.<ref name="Jewel" /> The [[2015]] sourcebook ''[[Fly Casual]]'' provided rules for playing a game of hintaro in ''Edge of the Empire''. To maintain for the players a sense of immersion in the [[roleplaying game]], the rules established a direct correspondence between several of the dice generally used in ''Edge of the Empire'' to resolve various situations and the [[in-universe]] chance cubes utilized by the player characters in hintaro.<ref name="Fly" />

An apparent contradiction exists regarding an illustration by [[Jeff Lee Johnson]] titled "Not Addicted If You're Winning"<ref name="Johnson">{{WebCite|url=https://jeffleejohnson.com/site/NotAddictedIfYoureWinning.html|text=Not Addicted If You're Winning|author=Jeff Lee Johnson|work=[https://jeffleejohnson.com Jeff Lee Johnson's Horror Gallery]|archivedate=20190806031323}}</ref> that was included in the section of ''Fly Casual'' describing the rules of hintaro. Contrary to the rules contained in the section, which specify that each hintaro player rolls at most two dice at a [[Time/Legends|time]], one of the hintaro players depicted in the illustration appears to be rolling a set of five dice at the same time.<ref name="Fly" /> The illustration was later reused for a card in the [[2016]] ''[[Redemption and Return]]'' expansion set of Fantasy Flight Games' ''[[Star Wars: The Card Game]]''.<ref name="Redemption" />
